---
title: "Find candidate new state and domain records"
format: html
---

Here we present a practical guide to the `flora_distribution_gap()` function of the `floraR` package. Given a genus or species of plants or algae, it compares the Brazilian states where specimens of the taxon have been recorded against the states officially listed in its [Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB)](https://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/consulta/) distribution, and flags the states not yet in FFB as **candidate new state records** - for example, a species listed by FFB only for Bahia, but with herbarium specimens from Pernambuco.

Georeferenced records are also placed in the six Brazilian **phytogeographic domains**, to flag candidate new domain records in the same way.

Keeping distributions complete is part of expanding the FFB monographs: each candidate is a lead for the specialist of the group to check.

## How the comparison works

1. **FFB side.** The officially listed states come from the locally cached FFB dataset (downloaded only when needed, as in [`flora_download()`](/articles/download_ffb_dataset.qmd)). For a **genus**, the states of all its species and infraspecific taxa are combined; for a **species**, those of the species and its infraspecific taxa. If the name is a **synonym** in FFB, the distribution of its accepted name is used.
2. **Occurrence evidence.** Brazilian records of the taxon are counted by state, from GBIF, REFLORA, and JABOT by default (see below), and their evidence is merged, so that a state reported by any of them is flagged.
3. **Comparison.** Every state with records that FFB does not list is flagged as a new state record candidate.

Occurrence databases record states as free text, in many spellings - GBIF alone uses `"Goiás"`, `"Go"`, `"Est. do Bahia"`, `"Paraiba"`, or `"Brasília"` for the Federal District. The place fields of every source are standardised with `std_place()` from the [barRoso](https://github.com/DBOSlab/barRoso) package, and matched to FFB state names before comparison; values that are not Brazilian states are ignored, as are REFLORA and JABOT specimens collected outside Brazil.

## Where the evidence comes from

| `sources` | What it reads | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `"gbif"` (default) | [GBIF](https://www.gbif.org), which aggregates most Brazilian herbaria. | Fast: all states are counted in a single request. The name is resolved among plants and algae only, so the records of its synonyms and infraspecific taxa are included, and homonyms in other kingdoms (e.g. the moth *Gracilaria*) are excluded. |
| `"reflora"` (default) | Specimens of the [Reflora Virtual Herbarium](https://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/reflora/herbarioVirtual/), via the [refloraR](https://github.com/DBOSlab/refloraR) package. | Read from the herbaria's archives (see *Keeping the downloaded archives* below). |
| `"jabot"` (default) | Specimens of the herbaria hosted by [JABOT](https://jabot.jbrj.gov.br), the Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden's herbarium system, via the [jabotR](https://github.com/DBOSlab/jabotR) package. | Read from the herbaria's archives (see below). |
| `"speciesLink"` | [speciesLink](https://specieslink.net) records. | Requires a free API key, created at speciesLink and passed as `specieslink_key` or set as the `SPECIESLINK_KEY` environment variable. |

### Keeping the downloaded archives (`keep_downloads`)

The REFLORA and JABOT archives are big: the first analysis downloads several gigabytes to two folders in your working directory, `reflora_download/` and `jabot_download/`, which takes a while. By default (`keep_downloads = TRUE`) these folders are **kept**, so any new analysis - for the same taxon or another one - reuses them instead of downloading everything again. Reading them still takes a few minutes per call, so to check several taxa, give them all in one call (see [Several taxa in one call](#several-taxa-in-one-call)): the archives are then read only once.

If you only need one analysis, or want to keep the working directory clean and light, set `keep_downloads = FALSE`: the folders are deleted once the analysis is finished.

```r
# Delete the REFLORA and JABOT archives after this analysis
gap <- flora_distribution_gap(taxon = "Luetzelburgia auriculata", keep_downloads = FALSE)
```

`refloraR` and `jabotR` are installed from GitHub; without them, REFLORA or JABOT is skipped with a message:

```r
remotes::install_github(c("DBOSlab/refloraR", "DBOSlab/jabotR"))
```

## Find candidate new state records for a species

```r
library(floraR)

gap <- flora_distribution_gap(taxon = "Luetzelburgia auriculata")
```

This returns a list of three tables - `gap$states`, `gap$domains`, and `gap$records` - and also saves them as the sheets of an `.xlsx` spreadsheet, with a self-contained HTML report, in the `flora_distribution_gap/` folder. `gap$states` has one row per Brazilian state with any evidence:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | Brazilian state. |
| `in_ffb_distribution` | Whether FFB already lists the state for the taxon. |
| `gbif_records`, `reflora_records`, `jabot_records`, `specieslink_records` | Number of records in the state, for each source queried. |
| `new_state_record_candidate` | `TRUE` for states with records that FFB does not list. |

The columns created by `floraR` are in lower case, while the fields taken from the source databases in `gap$records` keep their original Darwin Core names - `recordedBy`, `recordNumber`, `eventDate`, `institutionCode`, `catalogNumber`, `scientificName` (the identification), `decimalLatitude`, `decimalLongitude`, and so on. `gap$records` holds every georeferenced record, plus the records without coordinates from the candidate new states, with the candidates first.

For *Luetzelburgia auriculata*, FFB lists 14 states, and the specimens in GBIF, REFLORA, and JABOT point to five more - Alagoas, Paraná, Rio de Janeiro, Rio Grande do Sul, and São Paulo. Paraná and Rio de Janeiro are backed by all three sources (e.g. Paraná: 22 GBIF records, 10 REFLORA and 7 JABOT specimens), while Rio Grande do Sul rests on a single GBIF record.

## Check the records behind each candidate

Occurrence records are evidence to review, not proof: a record from a new state may be a cultivated plant, a misidentification, or a georeferencing error. The spreadsheet is built for a specialist to validate them (see [Validating the spreadsheet](#validating-the-spreadsheet)), and the HTML report lists the individual records found in each candidate state - collector and number, date, locality, herbarium and catalogue number, and the name under which the specimen was identified - each linked to the record itself, so that every candidate can be checked before it goes into FFB.

## Phytogeographic domains

Alongside states, the GBIF, REFLORA, and JABOT records that have coordinates are placed in the six Brazilian phytogeographic domains - Amazônia, Caatinga, Cerrado, Mata Atlântica, Pampa, and Pantanal - using IBGE's biome map (2019) bundled with `floraR`. A domain with records but not listed for the taxon in FFB is a **candidate new domain record**. Records GBIF flags with geospatial issues (such as zero coordinates, or coordinates outside the stated country) are left out.

```r
gap$domains                                          # one row per domain
gap$records[gap$records$new_domain_record_candidate, ]  # the records behind new domains
```

For *Luetzelburgia auriculata*, FFB lists the Amazônia, Caatinga, and Cerrado. Of its 1,134 georeferenced records - 745 from GBIF, 258 from REFLORA, and 131 from JABOT - 10, from Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, and Paraná, fall in the **Mata Atlântica**, a candidate new domain:

| Domain | In FFB | Georeferenced records | New domain candidate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Amazônia | yes | 12 | |
| Caatinga | yes | 766 | |
| Cerrado | yes | 299 | |
| Mata Atlântica | no | 10 | **yes** |

The HTML report maps every georeferenced record over the domains, coloured by status - click a point to see its collector, date, herbarium, and a link to the record:

![The georeferenced GBIF, REFLORA, and JABOT records of *Luetzelburgia auriculata* over the Brazilian phytogeographic domains, over the FFB domain colours: in yellow, the candidate new domain records in the Mata Atlântica; in red, a candidate new state record.](/figures/flora_distribution_gap_map.png){width=100%}

A record close to a domain boundary, or a single record in a new domain, deserves a closer look - it may be a cultivated plant or a georeferencing error. The domain analysis needs the `sf` package, and the map the `leaflet` package; set `domains = FALSE` to skip it.

## A whole genus, or selected states

For a genus, FFB's distribution is the union of all its species':

```r
gap_genus <- flora_distribution_gap(taxon = "Luetzelburgia")
```

To check only some states (full names or acronyms, with or without accents):

```r
gap_ne <- flora_distribution_gap(taxon = "Luetzelburgia auriculata",
                                 state = c("PE", "Paraiba", "Alagoas"))
```

## Validating the spreadsheet

Each spreadsheet is designed to be handed to a specialist of the group, who confirms the candidates before they go into FFB. **The specialist does not need to check every record**: the goal is to find **at least one voucher specimen** supporting each candidate new state or domain. Once a candidate has one voucher, it is supported, and the specialist moves on to the next one.

The spreadsheet has four sheets:

| Sheet | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `instructions` | The first sheet: what to do, the terms to use, a fictitious example, and the progress of the review. |
| `states` | One row per state, as in `gap$states`. For each candidate, `records_reviewed` and `vouchers_validated` count the specialist's work in `records`. |
| `domains` | The same for the phytogeographic domains. |
| `records` | The individual records, candidates first, each with `record_link` to the specimen. **The only sheet to fill in**, in its last two columns, `validation` and `comments`. |

What the specialist does:

1. In `states`, pick a row with `new_state_record_candidate = TRUE`.
2. In `records`, filter the column `state` to that state, and open `record_link` to see the specimen - its image, label, and identification.
3. In `validation`, choose one of three words from the drop-down list (below).
4. As soon as one record is `correct`, the state is supported: move on to the next candidate state. If the record is `incorrect` or `uncertain`, check the next record of the same state.
5. Do the same for the candidate domains, filtering `records` by `domain` and `new_domain_record_candidate = TRUE`. A record validated as `correct` counts for both its state and its domain.
6. Leave `validation` **empty** for the records not looked at: every filled cell counts as a reviewed record.

The terms of the `validation` column - always the same three words:

| `validation` | When to use it |
|---|---|
| `correct` | The specimen was checked: its identification is right and it was collected in that state or domain. It is a voucher for the new record. |
| `incorrect` | The specimen was checked: it is misidentified, or its locality or coordinates are wrong. It does not support the record. |
| `uncertain` | The specimen was checked, but it is impossible to decide (e.g. sterile material, poor image, unreadable label, difficult group). |
| *(empty)* | Not reviewed. |

The column `comments` is **optional** free text - filled in only when there is something to add. For example (fictitious records):

| `state` | `catalogNumber` | `validation` | `comments` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Piauí | XX0000001 | `incorrect` | Misidentified: it is *Genus alterus* |
| Piauí | XX0000002 | `uncertain` | Sterile; image too poor to confirm |
| Piauí | XX0000003 | `correct` | |
| Piauí | XX0000004 | | *(not reviewed: Piauí already has a voucher)* |
| Pará | XX0000005 | `uncertain` | Possibly an undescribed species - needs further study |

The `instructions` sheet sums up the progress - records reviewed, how many `correct`, `incorrect`, and `uncertain`, and how many candidate states and domains already have a voucher - and Excel updates these counts, and those of `states` and `domains`, as the specialist works. Do not rename the sheets or columns, since the counters depend on them. Every sheet has filters on its header, and the header row and the taxon column stay frozen while scrolling. The `validation` and `comments` columns and the counters exist only in the spreadsheet, not in the tables returned in R.

## Several taxa in one call

`taxon` also takes a vector of names - species, genera, or both. Reading the REFLORA and JABOT archives is the slow step, and it is done only **once** for all of them, so one call with ten species is much faster than ten separate calls:

```r
gap_many <- flora_distribution_gap(taxon = c("Luetzelburgia auriculata",
                                             "Luetzelburgia bahiensis",
                                             "Luetzelburgia praecox"))

# The candidates of all three species, in one table
gap_many$states[gap_many$states$new_state_record_candidate, ]
```

Each taxon is analysed separately, and gets its own spreadsheet and HTML report in `dir`, named after it - `flora_distribution_gap_Luetzelburgia_auriculata.xlsx`, `flora_distribution_gap_Luetzelburgia_bahiensis.html`, and so on. The returned `states`, `domains`, and `records` tables stack the rows of all taxa, told apart by their `taxon` column. A name that fails (e.g. a misspelling) is reported and skipped, without stopping the others.

## Taxa with nothing new

A taxon whose records all fall within its FFB distribution - no candidate new state, no candidate new domain - needs no FFB update, so it gets **no** spreadsheet or detailed report. Instead, all such taxa of a call are listed together in one simple page, `__no_new_records_report.html` in `dir` (the leading underscores keep it at the top of the folder). For each taxon it shows its FFB states and domains, the number of records found in each source, and a conclusion:

| Conclusion | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Within FFB distribution - no update needed | Records were found, and all of them are in states and domains FFB already lists. |
| No records found - check the name | The databases returned nothing, so the result says nothing about the distribution - often a misspelt name. |

So, after checking a list of taxa, the folder holds one spreadsheet and one report per taxon that needs an FFB update, and this single page for the rest. The rows of the taxa with nothing new are still returned by the function.

## Choose the sources

```r
# A quick check with GBIF only, without the REFLORA and JABOT archives
gap_gbif <- flora_distribution_gap(taxon = "Luetzelburgia auriculata", sources = "gbif")

# Brazilian herbaria only
gap_herbaria <- flora_distribution_gap(taxon = "Luetzelburgia auriculata",
                                       sources = c("reflora", "jabot"))

# Adding speciesLink, with your API key in the SPECIESLINK_KEY environment variable
gap_splink <- flora_distribution_gap(taxon = "Luetzelburgia auriculata",
                                     sources = c("gbif", "reflora", "jabot", "speciesLink"))
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `taxon` | One or more genus or species names of plants or algae; see [Several taxa in one call](#several-taxa-in-one-call). |
| `state` | Optional Brazilian states to restrict the check to. `NULL` (default) checks all. |
| `sources` | Any of `"gbif"`, `"reflora"`, `"jabot"`, `"speciesLink"`. Default: `c("gbif", "reflora", "jabot")`. |
| `keep_downloads` | If `TRUE` (default), keep the downloaded `reflora_download/` and `jabot_download/` folders for later analyses; if `FALSE`, delete them afterwards. |
| `specieslink_key` | speciesLink API key. Defaults to the `SPECIESLINK_KEY` environment variable. |
| `domains` | If `TRUE` (default), also place georeferenced records in the phytogeographic domains. Requires the `sf` package. |
| `max_coordinates` | Maximum number of georeferenced GBIF records read for the domain analysis. Default `5000`. |
| `version` | FFB dataset version to compare against. Default `"latest"`. |
| `save`, `dir` | Save each taxon's result as an `.xlsx` spreadsheet ready for validation (see [Validating the spreadsheet](#validating-the-spreadsheet)), named `flora_distribution_gap_<taxon>.xlsx`, and where; taxa with nothing new get none (see [Taxa with nothing new](#taxa-with-nothing-new)). |
| `html_report`, `open_report` | Write the HTML report, and (with `open_report = TRUE`) open it in the browser. |
| `verbose` | Print progress messages. Default `TRUE`. |

## Additional Tips

- A single record in a new state deserves more scrutiny than dozens: check the specimen, its identification, and whether it was cultivated.
- Some taxa have no state-level distribution in FFB at all (as for some marine algae); the function then says so, and every state with records is flagged.
- The HTML report requires the `rmarkdown`, `DT`, and `htmltools` packages. Without them, the report is skipped with a message and the spreadsheet is still saved.
